title: A raw free-T3/free-T4 ratio term adds no robust cross-cycle pulse prediction beyond marginal thyroid measures
abstract: Can a joint thyroid-hormone representation recover pulse information missed by marginal hormone models? In separately sampled NHANES 2007–08 and 2011–12 adults, a source-fitted free-T3/free-T4 ratio term changed target weighted resting-pulse MSE from 131.370583 to 131.359698 bpm², a -0.0083% change. The source-refit/target-PSU 95% interval for augmented-minus-baseline MSE was [-0.315690, 0.518605]. Source group cross-validation worsened and euthyroid-restricted results changed sign. A post-primary spline ratio improved target MSE by 0.479 bpm², but source-refit uncertainty included harm and euthyroid restriction worsened performance. These exploratory data provide no robust incremental predictive evidence for the primary ratio specification; they do not prove equivalence or absence of thyroid physiology.
